title: Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy, Interval Debulking & HIPEC: Trial Evidence, Peritoneal Cancer Index and Heated Perfusion
subject: ss-gynaecological-oncology
refs: Berek & Hacker's Gynecologic Oncology 7th Edition Ch 16
DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology 11th Edition Ch 85
van Driel WJ et al. Hyperthermic Intraperitoneal Chemotherapy in Ovarian Cancer. NEJM 2018

steps.say: The oncological equivalence of neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by interval debulking surgery compared to upfront primary debulking has been confirmed in multiple phase three randomized trials.
steps.tx: Four landmark phase III trials (**EORTC 55971**, **CHORUS trial**, JCOG0602, and SCORPION) demonstrated that neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by **interval debulking surgery (IDS)** achieves **equivalent overall survival** compared to primary debulking surgery in bulky Stage IIIC and IV epithelial ovarian cancer.

vis.caption: Complete visible clearance is the goal of ovarian debulking. Illustration: StewardMD original.
vis.alt: Illustration showing surgical field after maximal debulking of advanced ovarian cancer.

steps.say: Administering neoadjuvant chemotherapy before cytoreductive surgery significantly diminishes perioperative morbidity and enhances complete surgical cytoreduction rates.
steps.tx: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by interval debulking achieves a significant **reduction in perioperative morbidity**, markedly lower postoperative mortality (<1%), reduced requirements for intensive care, and a significantly **higher R0 resection rate** compared to upfront primary surgery in advanced disease across multicenter international cohorts.

nodes.label: Diagnose advanced Stage IIIC/IV ovarian cancer with high tumor burden
Administer 3 cycles of neoadjuvant carboplatin AUC 6 and paclitaxel 175 mg/m2
Confirm biochemical and CT radiological response without progression
Perform interval debulking surgery targeting complete macroscopic R0 resection

steps.say: To prevent unnecessary laparotomies in patients whose disease is unresectable, staging laparoscopy and the Fagotti scoring algorithm provide objective resectability assessment.
steps.tx: Diagnostic **staging laparoscopy** utilizes the **Fagotti score** (evaluating 7 parameters: omental cake, peritoneal carcinomatosis, diaphragmatic and mesenteric retraction, bowel and stomach infiltration, liver metastasis); a **Fagotti score >=8** reliably predicts incomplete cytoreduction with >90% accuracy, directing patients to neoadjuvant therapy.

rows: Massive omental infiltration extending to stomach spleen
Absent or only minimal omental nodules
Isolated small nodules or smooth peritoneum
Root of mesentery retracted with bowel clumped
Miliary serosal implants or deep subserosal nodules
Visible serosal infiltration of stomach or liver surface
Completely clear stomach and hepatic parenchyma

steps.say: Quantifying the anatomical extent of peritoneal carcinomatosis is critical for standardizing surgical planning and predicting cytoreductive success.
steps.tx: The Sugarbaker **Peritoneal Cancer Index (PCI)** divides the abdomen into 13 anatomical regions, scoring lesion size from 0 to 3 in each region (yielding a maximum **PCI maximum 39**). A high PCI score directly correlates with unresectability and worse progression-free survival.

left.title: Low to Moderate PCI (< 15-20)
points: Localized or limited regional peritoneal carcinomatosis
High probability of achieving complete R0 cytoreduction
Excellent candidate for complete surgical cytoreduction and HIPEC

right.title: Extensive PCI (> 20-25)
points: Diffuse involvement of small bowel mesentery and diaphragms
Significantly increased risk of leaving residual macroscopic disease
Higher rate of severe postoperative multi-organ morbidity

steps.say: The prospective Dutch OVHIPEC-1 phase three randomized trial established the therapeutic benefit of adding heated intraperitoneal chemotherapy at the time of interval debulking.
steps.tx: The landmark **OVHIPEC-1 trial** (van Driel 2018) demonstrated that adding hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (**HIPEC**) at the time of interval debulking surgery yielded a statistically significant **12-month overall survival benefit** (median OS 45.7 months vs 33.9 months) in Stage III ovarian cancer.

nodes.label: Patient undergoes 3 cycles of NACT followed by interval debulking
Surgeon achieves complete R0 or optimal (<1 cm) cytoreduction
Randomize intraoperatively to HIPEC perfusion vs surgery alone
HIPEC delivers significant 12-month improvement in median overall survival

steps.say: The delivery of heated intraperitoneal chemotherapy relies on rigorous pharmacological, temperature, and perfusate circulation standards.
steps.tx: The standard HIPEC protocol delivers heated **cisplatin 100 mg/m2** dissolved in isotonic dialysate circulated through a closed abdominopelvic circuit at a therapeutic temperature maintained strictly at **40 to 41 degrees C** for a continuous perfusion **duration 90 minutes** under close hemodynamic monitoring.

rows: Cisplatin 100 mg/m2 (50% initially, 25% at 30 min, 25% at 60 min)
Maintained strictly at 40.0 C to 41.5 C intra-abdominally
Increases tissue penetration and platinum cytotoxicity

steps.say: The therapeutic synergy of hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy derives from distinct thermal and pharmacokinetic mechanisms that overcome systemic chemotherapy barriers.
steps.tx: HIPEC relies on **hyperthermic synergy**, which impairs cellular DNA repair pathways, enhances platinum alkylation, and exploits the **peritoneal-plasma barrier** to achieve up to 20-fold higher local **peritoneal drug concentration** while limiting systemic haematological and renal toxicities throughout the body. Multidisciplinary tumour board review ensures optimal clinical staging and coordinates tailored surgical oncological interventions.

left.title: Thermal Enhancement Mechanism
points: Hyperthermia directly inhibits homologous recombination DNA repair
Increases microvascular permeability in microscopic tumor deposits
Sensitizes malignant cells to platinum-induced apoptosis

right.title: Peritoneal Pharmacokinetics
points: Peritoneal-plasma barrier retards systemic drug absorption
Local peritoneal concentration up to 20 times higher than serum
Eliminates microscopic residual cells floating in peritoneal fluid

steps.say: The application of hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy requires strict patient selection and must not be offered following upfront primary debulking outside clinical trials.
steps.tx: HIPEC is clinically validated exclusively following interval debulking after neoadjuvant therapy. The trial **omission in primary debulking** is supported by recent data showing no survival advantage when added during upfront surgery, while carrying a recognized **acute kidney injury risk** that requires vigilant perioperative hydration.
